questions.question:
**Read the below statement:**

1. Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India.

2. A candidate contesting for the post of the President of India is required to make a security deposit of ₹15,000.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **security deposit of ₹15,000** is mandatory for candidates contesting the election for the President of India, as per **Article 58 of the Constitution of India** and the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952.
 
• The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure at least one-sixth of the votes cast in the election.
 
• The security deposit ensures that only serious candidates participate in the election process.
 
• The election of the President of India is conducted by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
 
• As per the rules, the nomination paper must be supported by at least **50 proposers and 50 seconders** to ensure legitimacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement 1: Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India**

 
 
• The Solicitor General of India is the **second-highest law officer** in the country after the Attorney General of India.
 
• Unlike the Attorney General, the Solicitor General is not appointed directly by the President of India. Instead, the appointment is made by the **Union Government**, specifically by the Ministry of Law and Justice.
 
• The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General in performing legal duties and advises the government on legal matters.
 
• Therefore, **Statement 1 is incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Presidential Elections in India:**
 
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college through a proportional representation system using a single transferable vote.
 
• Every member of the electoral college casts their vote, and the candidate receiving the highest number of votes is elected.
 
• The process is governed by the provisions in **Articles 52 to 62** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Facts:**
 
 
• The President of India serves a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
• The eligibility criteria for candidates contesting the Presidential elections include being a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• In case of vacancy, the election must be held within six months.

questions.question:
Based on the given statements which option is **correct**:

**Statement I:** Mathura art produced images for both Indian and non-Indian patrons.

**Statement II:** Mathura art ignored nature-based themes in its sculptures.

options.text: Statement I and II both are Correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Only Statement I is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement I is correct:** Mathura art was a significant school of art during the Kushana period, producing sculptures for both Indian and non-Indian patrons, including images of Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Yakshas, and Jain Tirthankaras.
 
• Mathura art is renowned for its syncretic style, blending indigenous Indian artistic traditions with Greco-Roman influences.
 
• It catered to diverse religious communities like Buddhists, Jains, and Hindus, reflecting its inclusive nature and wide patronage.
 
• Mathura art produced sculptures for Buddhist stupas in India and beyond, including regions such as Central Asia, showcasing its appeal to non-Indian patrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement II is incorrect:** Mathura art did not ignore nature-based themes. In fact:

 
 
• It prominently featured nature-inspired motifs such as trees, animals, and floral designs in its sculptures.
 
• Yakshas and Yakshinis, celestial beings associated with nature and fertility, were frequently depicted in Mathura sculptures.
 
• Nature was often used symbolically in Buddhist and Jain art, such as the Bodhi tree representing Buddha's enlightenment.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Mathura Art:**
 
 
• Mathura art evolved during the Kushana period and served as a major center of artistic activity.
 
• It is characterized by red sandstone sculptures with intricate detailing and bold expressions.
 
• The art form emphasized realism and depicted human and divine figures with naturalistic features and elaborate ornamentation.
 
• Notable examples include the seated Buddha statues and images of Hindu deities like Vishnu and Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Gandhara Art:**
 
 
• While Mathura art represented indigenous Indian styles, Gandhara art reflected strong Greco-Roman influences.
 
• Mathura sculptures were made of red sandstone, whereas Gandhara sculptures predominantly used grey schist stone.

questions.question: In freestyle wrestling, which of the following actions can result in a technical point for the wrestler?

options.text: Running out of the mat deliberately

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Performing a successful takedown**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A takedown is a critical technique in freestyle wrestling that allows a wrestler to bring their opponent from a standing position to the mat and gain control.
 
• Performing a successful takedown awards the wrestler technical points, which depend on the skill level and execution of the move (usually 2 to 5 points).
 
• Common types of takedowns include single-leg takedown, double-leg takedown, and throws.
 
• In addition to scoring points, a takedown puts the wrestler in an advantageous position to attempt further scoring or pinning.
 
• Freestyle wrestling emphasizes both offensive and defensive techniques, with takedowns being one of the primary methods of scoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Running out of the mat deliberately**

 
 
• Running out of the mat is considered a form of passive wrestling or avoiding engagement, which can lead to penalties.
 
• Instead of gaining points, wrestlers may receive warnings or penalties for deliberately stepping out of the mat to escape an opponent’s hold or avoid engagement.
 
• In some cases, referees may award points to the opponent if this action is deemed intentional.
 
 
 
• **Holding the opponent's singlet**

questions.question: The term "pleiotropy" refers to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One gene affects multiple traits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pleiotropy** refers to a situation where a single gene affects multiple phenotypic traits.
 
• This occurs because the gene encodes a product (such as a protein) that is involved in multiple biological processes.
 
• Examples of pleiotropy include the gene responsible for sickle-cell anemia, which affects red blood cell shape and provides resistance to malaria.
 
• Pleiotropic effects can be observed in both normal physiological processes and genetic disorders.
 
• Pleiotropy is a fundamental concept in genetics and demonstrates how genes can have far-reaching effects on an organism's phenotype.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Multiple genes affect one trait**

 
 
• This describes a phenomenon known as **polygenic inheritance**, where a trait is governed by two or more genes.
 
• Examples include human height, skin color, and eye color, which result from the combined effect of several genes.
 
• Polygenic traits often show continuous variation, unlike pleiotropic traits, which are influenced by a single gene.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Gene mutation in one allele**
 
 
• This refers to a mutation in one copy of a gene (allele) that can affect its function.
 
• Such mutations can lead to genetic disorders if the mutated allele is dominant or if the condition is recessive and both alleles are affected.
 
• While this is a distinct genetic concept, it does not describe pleiotropy.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Gene duplication**
 
 
• Gene duplication is an evolutionary process where a segment of DNA containing a gene is copied, resulting in multiple copies of that gene in the genome.
 
• This can lead to the evolution of new gene functions or increased gene dosage but is unrelated to pleiotropy.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Pleiotropy:**
 
 
• Pleiotropy is critical for understanding the complexity of genetic interactions and how single genes can have multiple impacts on an organism's physiology and development.
 
• It is also significant in studying diseases with pleiotropic effects, such as Marfan syndrome, where a single gene mutation affects the connective tissue throughout the body.

questions.question: How are Money Bills handled in both Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures with bicameralism under the Constitution?

options.text: Rajya Sabha must approve Money Bills within 14 days
In States, the Legislative Council can amend a Money Bill within 14 days
Both Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils have equal powers on Money Bills
Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days**__.

__
 
• Under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Once the Lok Sabha passes a Money Bill, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, but the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it.
 
• The Rajya Sabha must return the Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with or without recommendations within a period of 14 days. If not returned within this period, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• In the case of State Legislatures with bicameralism, the Legislative Council can only make recommendations to the Legislative Assembly on Money Bills and must return the Bill within 14 days.
 
• The powers of the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Councils on Money Bills are limited to recommendations, and the final decision rests with the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assembly, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Money Bill deals exclusively with matters listed in Article 110(1) of the Constitution, such as taxation, borrowing, expenditure, and matters incidental to these.
 
• The distinction between Money Bills and other financial Bills is significant because it limits the role of the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils in the legislative process.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Legislative Assembly is the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

• **Inertia** is the property of matter that causes it to resist changes in its state of motion or rest unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• It is a fundamental concept of classical mechanics, based on **Newton's First Law of Motion**, which states that "an object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion continues in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force."
 
• The difficulty in starting the motion of a heavy box is due to its **inertia of rest**, which resists any change from a stationary state.
 
• Similarly, the difficulty in stopping the box once it is moving is due to its **inertia of motion**, which resists any change in its current velocity.
 
• The larger the mass of an object, the greater its inertia, which is why heavier objects are harder to start or stop in motion.

• While conservation of energy is a fundamental concept in physics, it does not directly explain the difficulty in starting or stopping the motion of a heavy object.

**Consider the following statements:**

1. Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another.

2. Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment.

Which of the above is/are **correct?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1: Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another** – Article 139A of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases involving the same or substantially the same question of law from one High Court to another to ensure uniformity in decisions.
 
• This provision is aimed at eliminating conflicting judgments by different High Courts on the same legal matter, thereby ensuring consistency in the interpretation of laws across the country.
 
• **Statement 2: Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment** – The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Article 139A to the Indian Constitution. This amendment is often referred to as the "mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• Article 139A allows the Supreme Court to withdraw cases from one or more High Courts if it feels that these cases involve a substantial question of law of general importance.
 
• Both statements are correct, as Article 139A was indeed introduced by the 42nd Amendment, and it authorizes the Supreme Court to transfer cases between High Courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment of 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "mini-Constitution," this amendment brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added several articles, including Article 139A, and amended many existing provisions to strengthen the central government's powers.
 
• Key changes included the addition of the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and the insertion of the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" into the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court’s Powers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to transfer cases between High Courts or withdraw cases from High Courts to itself if substantial questions of law are involved.
 
• This provision ensures uniformity in the interpretation of laws across different jurisdictions in India.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Transfers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• This article is critical for maintaining judicial discipline and consistency in legal interpretations by higher judiciary bodies.
 
• Such transfers are often considered in cases involving constitutional interpretation or significant questions of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Role of High Courts:**
 
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in India, but their decisions may differ based on regional contexts.
 
• Article 139A ensures that conflicting decisions on similar issues are avoided by centralizing the matter in the Supreme Court.

questions.question: What is the value of ((0.1×0.1×0.1+0.03×0.03×0.03))/((0.3×0.3×0.3+0.09×0.09×0.09))
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Observe the relationship between the numerator and the denominator.

Each term in the denominator is exactly 3 times the corresponding term in the numerator.

Expression = (0.1³ + 0.03³) ÷ [(3 × 0.1)³ + (3 × 0.03)³]

⇒ 1 ÷ 3³ = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ 1 ÷ 27 ≈ 0.037

**∴ The correct answer is 0.037.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (0.1 × 0.1 × 0.1 + 0.03 × 0.03 × 0.03) ÷ (0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 + 0.09 × 0.09 × 0.09)

**Formula Used:**

(x × y)ⁿ = xⁿ × yⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = 0.1³ + 0.03³

⇒ Denominator = 0.3³ + 0.09³

⇒ Denominator = (3 × 0.1)³ + (3 × 0.03)³

⇒ Denominator = 3³ × 0.1³ + 3³ × 0.03³

⇒ Denominator = 27 × (0.1³ + 0.03³)

⇒ Expression = (0.1³ + 0.03³) ÷ [27 × (0.1³ + 0.03³)]

⇒ Expression = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ 1 ÷ 27 = 0.037037...

**∴ The correct answer is 0.037.**

**__Additional Information__**

Laws of Exponents

When terms are multiplied and raised to a common power, the power distributes directly to both numbers: (xy)ⁿ = xⁿ × yⁿ. This allows easy extraction of common multiples from complex decimals.

Algebraic Simplification

In simplification problems involving decimals that look similar, always check if the denominator is a direct multiple of the numerator before calculating the actual cubes or squares.

Recurring Decimals

Fractions like 1 ÷ 27 result in non-terminating, repeating decimals. The value 1 ÷ 27 equals 0.037037037..., which is generally rounded off to 0.037 as given in the exam options.
</p

questions.question: Three numbers are such that when the average of any two of them is added to the third, the results obtained are 180, 168, and 150, respectively. What is the average of the original three numbers?

Summing the three given results evaluates to 2 times the sum of the three numbers.

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 a + b + 2c = 360
 
 
 2a + b + c = 336
 
 
 a + 2b + c = 300

 Average = 83

⇒ a + b + 2c = 360 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ (b + c) ÷ 2 + a = 168

questions.question: A cyclist travels from City A to City B at an average speed of 20 km/h and takes 4 hours. If they want to complete the same journey in 2.5 hours, by what amount (in km/h) should they increase their average speed?

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

⇒ 20 × 4 = S₂ × 2.5

⇒ S₂ = 80 ÷ 2.5 = 32 km/h

Increase in speed = S₂ − S₁ = 32 − 20 = 12 km/h

Initial Time (T₁) = 4 hours

⇒ S₂ = 32 km/h
